info.title: MetaTracer
info.description: Sensitive metadata discovery for authorized security audits. Authentication is optional (METATRACER_AUTH_ENABLED): when off, bind to localhost / trusted networks only.

get.description:
Liveness probe for the Docker HEALTHCHECK (TASK-07, subtask 7.3.5).

Deliberately stateless: it reveals no configuration, counters or
version beyond what the API schema already exposes.

Local run history, newest first (TASK-08). Not a multi-tenant dashboard.

TASK-21 (v2.4): cursor pagination. The repo fetches ``limit + 1`` rows so
``has_more`` needs no extra query; ``next_cursor`` is the last row's
``(started_at, id)`` anchor when more rows exist. Keyset stays stable when
a new run lands between two pages — nothing is duplicated or dropped.
``limit`` remains bounded by ``_MAX_HISTORY``.

schema.description: Opaque keyset anchor from a previous page's next_cursor (<started_at_iso>_<run_id>)

post.description:
Start a scan in the background; the run_id is known immediately.

The scope gate and the single-scan lock live in the orchestrator and raise
synchronously inside :meth:`ScanOrchestratorService.start_scan`, so the
403/409 answers happen within this request — never after a 202.

get.description: Status, counters, timestamps and the failed/skipped asset issues.

Server-sent events stream of ProgressEvent (one JSON object per event).

The bus replays the run's full history into the subscriber queue, so a
client connecting late or reconnecting still sees every stage; the stream
closes after the terminal ``completed``/``failed`` event.

Findings in report order (critical -> info, unclassified last).

Filters are exploration-only: exported reports stay complete. Invalid enum
values are rejected by FastAPI with 422.

Regenerate the report from the database and serve it as an attachment.

The file name comes from the exporter (sanitized slug + run id +
timestamp), never from raw user input.
List persisted scopes, newest first (TASK-08-style local data).

post.description: Create a scope; ``name`` must be unique case-insensitively (409).

put.description: Full replacement (no PATCH); the same name-uniqueness rule applies.

delete.description: Delete a scope; persisted runs keep their own copied scope.

post.description:
Import scopes from a portable JSON file (idempotent, non-destructive).

The body is the raw portable-scopes JSON (no multipart, keeping the
dependency list closed, same postura as ``import_kb_endpoint`` in TASK-17).
The file format is the portable scopes contract of
:mod:`metatracer.scopes.portable` (``format_version`` 1, ``scopes`` list).
Existing names are skipped — importing the same file twice creates nothing
new. Invalid files are rejected with 422 (never partially inserted, never
reassigned).

get.description: One aggregated snapshot of runs, findings, top domains and agent usage.
List the in-memory queue, newest first. Read-only: never writes.

delete.description:
Delete one notification by list index (manual cleanup).

404 when the index is out of range (or the entry was already deleted):
events are ephemeral, so a stale index can never resolve to another event.

put.description:
Create, or replace, the operator feedback for one finding.

The current severity of the finding at vote time is recorded as
``severity_before`` so the few-shot example stays truthful even if the
finding is re-classified later.

get.description: Return the active feedback of one finding, if any.

delete.description: Remove the operator feedback (the memory forgets that finding).

Rank the historical findings most similar to ``q``.

The retriever is built from the app's engine/factory on first use and
reused for the life of the process. ``finding_type``, when given, must be
a closed enum value; anything else is rejected with 422 by the Query
dependency (FastAPI validates the Literal-style check below).

post.description:
Export the historical precedents as a downloadable portable KB JSON.

The writer streams to a temporary file (never persists a copy on the
server); the operator downloads it and owns the file. Only the portable-KB
contract fields leave the machine — never run/asset ids, raw metadata or
bytes.

Import a portable KB JSON into the local database (idempotent).

Rows whose original finding id was already imported are skipped; nothing
is deleted. ``finding_type``/``severity`` are validated against the
closed enums and an invalid file is rejected with 422 (never reassigned).
The body is the raw portable JSON (no multipart, keeping the dependency
list closed).

Verify credentials, create a fresh session, set cookies.

Rotation: every successful login creates a NEW session row and deletes
the user's previous sessions (one active session per user keeps the
surface tiny; a re-login also invalidates a stale stolen cookie).
Unknown usernames burn one PBKDF2 verification to even out timing.

Login-CSRF (review 2026-09-18): a cross-site POST could log the victim
into the attacker's account (or rotate away a legitimate session with
SameSite=Lax). Mitigation: the double-submit check applies here too —
the CSRF cookie is issued by any page render (middleware-protected pages
and /login itself always fetch a fresh one via _ensure_csrf_cookie), so
an attacker without that random value cannot mount login-CSRF.

schema.title: Response Login Endpoint Api Auth Login Post

post.description:
Delete the session row (if any) and expire both cookies.

CSRF applies here too (review 2026-09-18): a cross-site POST could force
a logout (session DoS). The caller holds a valid session anyway, so the
same double-submit check costs nothing.

schema.title: Response Logout Endpoint Api Auth Logout Post

get.description: Diagnostic: who is the caller (never exposes hashes or tokens).

schema.title: Response Me Endpoint Api Auth Me Get

post.description:
Create the first operator with the one-shot console setup token.

Reachable only when ALL of these hold: auth ON, no user provisioned from
the environment, no user in the table and a live setup token on
``app.state``. Any other posture answers 404 (setup disabled) or 409
(already has users) so the endpoint never becomes a standing account
factory. On success it behaves like a login: fresh session + CSRF
cookies, and the token is burned from memory.

schema.title: Response Setup Endpoint Api Auth Setup Post

post.description:
Redeem an invitation code: create the user, mark the code used, log in.

The code is looked up by its SHA-256 (only hashes are persisted). Unknown,
used and expired codes all answer the SAME generic 401, and an unknown
code burns one PBKDF2 verification so the response time does not reveal
whether a code hash exists (same technique as the login dummy hash).
The redeemed user gets the role recorded in the code by its creator.

schema.title: Response Register Endpoint Api Auth Register Post

get.description: List accounts (no hash material), newest first.

post.description: Create an account directly (operator-only; CSRF enforced upstream).

patch.description:
Change a user's role, guarding the last-operator invariant.

Demoting the only operator would leave the installation without anyone
able to administer users, so it is refused (409). Any other change is
allowed — including an operator promoting a viewer.

delete.description:
Delete an account (sessions cascade via the migration's ON DELETE).

Self-deletion is refused (nobody locks themselves out) and the last
operator cannot be deleted (409) — the installation must keep one admin.

get.description: List invitation metadata (never the codes), newest first.

post.description:
Mint one single-use invitation; the code is shown EXACTLY here, once.

Only the SHA-256 of the code is persisted (same technique as session
tokens), so the plaintext exists in this response and nowhere else — not
in the database, not in logs, not in later GET responses.

delete.description: Revoke an invitation by physical delete; idempotent 404 when gone.

DashboardStatsResponse.description:
GET /api/stats: one aggregated snapshot of the local data (TASK-11).

Read-only and agent-agnostic: built entirely from persisted counters, so
it works with zero runs and with zero agent_log rows.

FeedbackCreate.title: FeedbackCreate
FeedbackCreate.description: PUT body: the operator's correction of one finding's severity.

FeedbackResponse.title: FeedbackResponse
FeedbackResponse.description: One persisted feedback row, returned on GET/PUT.

FeedbackVote.title: FeedbackVote
FeedbackVote.description:
Operator correction direction (TASK-13, v2.1+).

``up`` means the human considers the finding more severe than the model
said; ``down`` means less severe. Values are the lowercase wire strings.

FindingResponse.description: One finding card, mapped 1:1 from the ReportBuilder entry (parity).

ImportResponse.description: Number of rows actually inserted by a portable-KB import (TASK-17).

InvitationCreate.title: InvitationCreate
InvitationCreate.description: POST /api/invitations body; ``ttl_seconds`` defaults to the instance TTL.

InvitationCreatedResponse.title: InvitationCreatedResponse

InvitationResponse.title: InvitationResponse

NotificationListResponse.title: NotificationListResponse
NotificationListResponse.description: GET /api/notifications: the in-memory queue, newest first.

NotificationResponse.title: NotificationResponse
NotificationResponse.description:
One terminal-run notification (TASK-12, v2.0).

``kind`` reuses the ``run.status`` enum (``completed`` | ``failed``) and
travels lowercase per the data contract; ``error_message`` is present only
for ``failed`` (the orchestrator already sanitized it).

RunListItem.title: RunListItem
RunListItem.description: One row of GET /api/runs (local history, TASK-08).

RunListResponse.title: RunListResponse
RunListResponse.description:
GET /api/runs: newest-first local history (TASK-08).

TASK-21 (v2.4): cursor pagination. ``total`` is the GLOBAL count of runs
matching the filter (untruncated, so the UI says "N runs" honestly);
``runs`` is the current page; ``has_more``/``next_cursor`` drive the
prev/next UI.

RunStatusResponse.title: RunStatusResponse
RunStatusResponse.description:
GET /api/runs/{run_id}: status, counters, timestamps and asset issues.

``asset_issues`` feeds the collapsible "Asset issues" section of the
dashboard (6.4): the simplest place for it, since the page already polls
this endpoint.

ScanRequest.title: ScanRequest
ScanRequest.description:
Validated scan parameters; also the exact POST /api/runs body (6.3).

At least one target and one confirmed scope source are required, and the
scope is a deliberate operator input — it is never derived from the
targets. The scope source is exactly one of: manual `scope_domains`
(v1.x), a single saved `scope_id` (TASK-10, v2.0) or the union of many
saved scopes `scope_ids` (TASK-21, v2.4); never a mix. `scope_id` is
kept as an alias of ``scope_ids=[scope_id]`` at the boundary, so none of
the v2.0-v2.3 clients break. Export options are NOT part of this
contract: they are parameters of
:meth:`ScanOrchestratorService.scan`, so the API request body stays
exactly this model.

ScopeImportResponse.title: ScopeImportResponse
ScopeImportResponse.description: TASK-19 (v2.2): outcome of a portable-scopes import.

ScopeResponse.title: ScopeResponse
ScopeResponse.description: One persisted scope, with the domains actually stored (normalized).

SearchHit.title: SearchHit
SearchHit.description: One ranked hit, surface-safe: no run_id, no raw ids beyond finding_id.

UserResponse.title: UserResponse
UserResponse.description: One account, without any secret material.

UserRole.title: UserRole
UserRole.description:
Role of an installation user (TASK-24 single operator; TASK-25 multi-user).

``operator`` can do everything (create scopes, launch scans, feedback,
webhooks, manage users and invitations). ``viewer`` is read-only
(dashboards, reports, exports). Values are the lowercase wire strings,
like every other closed enum.

UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate
UserUpdate.description: PATCH /api/users/{id} body: role changes only (passwords stay private).

WebhookCreate.title: WebhookCreate
WebhookCreate.description: POST /api/webhooks body. URL is HTTPS-only; everything else optional.

WebhookUpdate.title: WebhookUpdate
WebhookUpdate.description: PUT /api/webhooks/{id} body. All fields optional; unchanged when absent.
